subject: Error fitting zero-zero data using a zero inflated Poisson model

messages.author: 3f1b57241ff195d2
messages.subject: Error fitting zero-zero data using a zero inflated Poisson model
parts:
Hi

I am modelling point process data with INLA and have successfully been using family="poisson" in the inla call to fit my data, along the lines of Ch 13 and 14 of the SPDE tutorial. 

Now I would like to expand the standard Poisson model to a zero inflated Poisson model. However, using family="zeroinflatedpoissonX" with either of X=0,1,2 gives the error:

*** ERROR *** INLA.Data1: Poisson like data[0] (y,e) = (0,0) is void

I believe this is related to the fact that I have some occurrences with no observations (y=0), which are given zero weight (e=0) in my data. With family="poisson" this is handled nicely (simply setting the likelihood contribution to zero, I believe). 

Shouldn't the zero inflated model behave in the same way? Or is there a reason why 0-0 is not supported with the zero inflated models?

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error fitting zero-zero data using a zero inflated Poisson model
parts:
Hi Martin, 
I'm not sure a zero-inflated poison makes sense in that context. If you're trying to model detection probabilities, it comes out differently. 

With known probabilities it's in our point processes with SPDEs paper, for unknown detection probability, you need to make use of strong information about the measurement protocol. A good example is this paper https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06013

Best wishes,

Dan 

Sent from my iPad

messages.author: 3f1b57241ff195d2
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error fitting zero-zero data using a zero inflated Poisson model
parts:
Hi again and thank you for your kind reply.

I'm not really that interested the detection probabilities themselves, but merely in using a model fitting the data better. I have looked at your paper, but as my interest is not primarily in estimation of these, I am not sure that is the way to go. I am considering a zero-inflated model as zero counts may indeed appear for two different reasons, and when summarising the counts in the data there are clearly much more zeros than would be expected under a Poisson model. 

I have given this some serious though and I still think a zero-inflated Poisson model would make sense for point process data, at least how it is handled in INLA and the SPDE tutorial (ch 13-14) where the counts are aggregated to tiles using Voronoi triangulation. Using a zero-inflated model for this data would then amount to fitting a zero-inflated Poisson distribution to the counts in the tiles, rather than a regular Poisson distribution. Or am I missing something? How do you mean that a zero-inflated model does not make sense in this context?

The (y=0, e=0) points should make no contribution to the likelihood and be handled as for the regular Poisson likelihood, I believe? This is possibly related to the issue raised and solved in this old thread: https://groups.google.com/forum/embed/?parenturl=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.r-inla.org%2F&service=jotspot&ul=1&theme=default&place=forum%2Fr-inla-discussion-group&showpopout=true&showsearch=true#!searchin/r-inla-discussion-group/(0$2C0)$20is$20void/r-inla-discussion-group/PwKfQaNleU8/0hSrs6QmBtsJ 


Best regards,

Martin
